title.narrative: Strengthening Macroeconomic Resilience and Transparency Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The program aims to build on progress toward macroeconomic stability and sustainable growth following the economic crisis by strengthening public expenditure management, improving revenue collection, and fostering private sector participation. This includes enhancing the management, transparency, and accountability of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), strengthening the legal and institutional framework for public-private partnerships (PPPs), and improving the pipeline of climate-related projects, including those implemented through PPPs.

description.narrative: Policy Action/s as listed by the project staff.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: 1.3. To improve fiscal accountability and transparency, parliamentary oversight, and cash management, MOF: (i) Issued a circular requiring all extra-budgetary non-statutory funds to either obtain Parliamentary approval or be closed by 31 July 2025; and (ii) Issued a circular mandating all statutory funds to submit annual performance and financial reports to the Ministry of Finance, starting with fiscal year 2024 to be submitted by 31 March 2025.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: To ensure the efficient use of public funds, promote value for money, competitiveness and transparency, and strengthen accountability in public sector spending, the National Procurement Commission: (i) Approved and published the comprehensive and legally enforceable Procurement Guidelines - 2024 on Goods, Works, and Non-Consulting Services ;b and (ii) Published on its official website the National Procurement Manual on Goods, Works, and Non-Consulting Services to help operationalize the provisions of the procurement guidelines and strengthen implementation capacity across procuring entities.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: To minimize deviations between fiscal forecasts and outcomes, and to comply with the PFM Act, MOF published the inaugural Fiscal Risk Statement (FRS), which will present a comprehensive annual assessment of macroeconomic and fiscal risks and contingent liabilities, including risks posed from disasters and climate change.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: To strengthen digital public financial management and improve transparency, operational efficiency, and fiduciary control over public finances, MOF upgraded its core Integrated Treasury Management Information System (ITMIS) to include modules for budget planning, budget appropriation, purchasing, expenditure, treasury management, general ledger, and revenue functionalities in 171 out of 172 agencies.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: To strengthen institutional coordination, improve efficiency of public expenditure and operationalize the Public Financial Management (PFM) Act 2024, the Ministry of Finance (MOF): (i) Formally appointed an expert committee, co-chaired by two Deputy Secretaries of the Treasury, to oversee the preparation and consolidation of financial regulations under the PFM Act 2024; (ii) Issued a circular requiring all MOF departments to draft the subsidiary regulations to operationalize the PFM Act; and (iii) Established a technical working group comprising Treasury representatives to ensure effective consultation and coordination in the drafting of the financial regulations.

Reform area: Efficiency in public expenditure management improved
Outcome: b. Proportion of statutory and non-statutory funds submitting annual performance and financial reports to MOF increases to 90%
Description: To strengthen the integration of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into the national planning and budgeting system and improve overall monitoring and reporting of budgetary allocations on the SDGs including SDG 5 on achieving gender equality and empowering women and girls, in particular, the Ministry of Finance: (i) Issued a circular requiring line ministries to tag budget submissions in accordance with the SDG Budget Coding and Tagging methodology; and (ii) Published the SDG Budget Tagging Analysis Report for the 2025 Budget, including an analysis of budget allocations to SDG 5 on gender equality.

Reform area: Enabling environment for private sector participation strengthened
Outcome: Audited financial statements of 47 major SOEs published annually (baseline: no audited financial statements published as of 2024; source: MOF/Department of Public Enterprises website or official publications)
Description: To improve investor confidence, attract private investment, and enhance transparency and accountability in establishing a clear legal framework for well-structured and fiscally prudent public-private partnerships (PPPs), MOF published on its official website a draft PPP Bill for public consultation, which (i) sets out the powers of the National Agency for PPPs, which will serve as the central coordinating body for the development, implementation, oversight, and promotion of PPP projects in line with national policy and international best practices; and (ii) sets a clear and predictable legal framework to facilitate private investments in PPPs, strengthen investor protections, and ensure public sector support for strategic investment projects.

Reform area: Enabling environment for private sector participation strengthened
Outcome: Audited financial statements of 47 major SOEs published annually (baseline: no audited financial statements published as of 2024; source: MOF/Department of Public Enterprises website or official publications)
Description: To strengthen the enabling environment for private sector engagement in climate action, and to promote a cross-sectoral approach to climate action that contributes to broader socio-economic transformation: (i) The Government of Sri Lanka submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change its updated, gender-responsive Nationally Determined Contribution 2025 under the Paris Agreement, which aligns mitigation and adaptation priorities with national development objectives; and (ii) The Cabinet approved a national Climate Finance Strategy to guide the mobilization, management, and tracking of climate-related public and private financial flows, aligned with the country's NDC targets and medium-term fiscal strategy.

Reform area: Enabling environment for private sector participation strengthened
Outcome: Audited financial statements of 47 major SOEs published annually (baseline: no audited financial statements published as of 2024; source: MOF/Department of Public Enterprises website or official publications)
Description: To strengthen the institutional framework for managing fiscal risks from SOEs and increase the oversight of state-owned banks, MOF: (i) Secured Cabinet approval of the Credit Risk Assessment Framework (CRAF) to guide the evaluation and management of fiscal risks associated with SOEs, in line with the Public Debt Management Act; and (ii) Established a specialized monitoring unit within the Department of Public Enterprises to monitor the performance of state-owned banks.

Reform area: Revenue mobilization strengthened
Outcome: Tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) improved to at least 15% of GDP (2024 baseline: 13% of GDP). Source: Department of Fiscal Policy and Department of National Budget IMF staff report)
Description: To implement the recommendations of the Tax Administration Diagnostic Assessment Tool (TADAT) to improve tax administration and compliance, in particular improve the coordination between key revenue institutions: (i) The Inland Revenue Department adopted a two-year Tax Compliance Improvement Strategy (TCIS), setting time-bound actions to enhance tax administration and enforcement. (ii) The Cabinet approved the establishment of the Revenue Management Administration Reform and Modernization Bureau under the Presidential Secretariat to lead modernization and institutional coordination efforts; (iii) The MoF formally established the Revenue Management Committee to oversee the development and implementation of revenue strategies consistent with the annual fiscal strategy statement as per the PFM Act.

Reform area: Revenue mobilization strengthened
Outcome: Tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) improved to at least 15% of GDP (2024 baseline: 13% of GDP). Source: Department of Fiscal Policy and Department of National Budget IMF staff report)
Description: To strengthen tax transparency, combat cross-border tax evasion and safeguard the national tax base, Cabinet approved Sri Lanka's proposed application for membership of the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes and the Government submitted a formal letter requesting membership.
